sanskrit: tathā viprekṣamāṇasya vanaṃ puṣpitapādapam vicinvataś ca vaidehīṃ kiṃ cic cheṣā niśābhavat
english: As he gazed about the grove with its flowering trees and searched for Vaidehī, only a small portion of the night remained.

sanskrit: ṣaḍaṅgavedaviduṣāṃ kratupravarayājinām śuśrāva brahmaghoṣāṃś ca virātre brahmarakṣasām
english: In the deep of night he heard the Vedic chanting of Brahma-rākṣasas — those versed in the six ancillaries of the Veda and sacrificers at the foremost rites.

sanskrit: atha maṅgalavāditraiḥ śabdaiḥ śrotramanoharaiḥ prābodhyata mahābāhur daśagrīvo mahābalaḥ
english: Then, with the auspicious sounds of musical instruments pleasing to ear and mind, the mighty-armed, greatly powerful Daśagrīva was awakened.

sanskrit: vibudhya tu yathākālaṃ rākṣasendraḥ pratāvapān srastamālyāmbaradharo vaidehīm anvacintayat
english: Awakening at the proper hour, the lord of rākṣasas yawned and stretched; his garlands and garments dishevelled, he turned his mind to Vaidehī.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ niyuktas tasyāṃ ca madanena madotkaṭaḥ na sa taṃ rākṣasaḥ kāmaṃ śaśākātmani gūhitum
english: Mightily goaded by the god of love and overcome with passion for her, that rākṣasa could not conceal the desire within himself.

sanskrit: sa sarvābharaṇair yukto bibhrac chriyam anuttamām tāṃ nagair vividhair juṣṭāṃ sarvapuṣpaphalopagaiḥ
english: Adorned with every ornament and bearing an unrivalled splendour, he set out toward that garden frequented by various trees laden with every fruit and flower,

sanskrit: vṛtāṃ puṣkariṇībhiś ca nānāpuṣpopaśobhitām sadāmadaiś ca vihagair vicitrāṃ paramādbhutām
english: surrounded by lotus-ponds adorned with manifold blossoms, filled with perpetually intoxicated birds — a garden wondrous and supremely marvellous.

sanskrit: īhāmṛgaiś ca vividhaiḥ vṛtāṃ dṛṣṭimanoharaiḥ vīthīḥ saṃprekṣamāṇaś ca maṇikāñcanatoraṇāḥ
english: Encircled by diverse creatures delightful to the eye, and beholding the avenues with their archways of jewels and gold,

sanskrit: nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇāṃ phalaiḥ prapatitair vṛtām aśokavanikām eva prāviśat saṃtatadrumām
english: he entered the Aśoka grove — densely wooded, thronged with herds of various animals, and carpeted with fallen fruits.

sanskrit: aṅganāśatamātraṃ tu taṃ vrajantam anuvrajat mahendram iva paulastyaṃ devagandharvayoṣitaḥ
english: A full hundred women followed him as he walked — that descendant of Pulastya — just as the women of gods and gandharvas follow great Indra.

sanskrit: dīpikāḥ kāñcanīḥ kāś cij jagṛhus tatra yoṣitaḥ bālavyajanahastāś ca tālavṛntāni cāparāḥ
english: Some women there took up golden lamps, others held young fly-whisks in their hands, and yet others carried palm-leaf fans.

sanskrit: kāñcanair api bhṛṅgārair jahruḥ salilam agrataḥ maṇḍalāgrān asīṃś caiva gṛhyānyāḥ pṛṣṭhato yayuḥ
english: Some carried water in golden pitchers and went before him; others took up broad-edged swords and followed behind.

sanskrit: kā cid ratnamayīṃ pātrīṃ pūrṇāṃ pānasya bhāminī dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇenaiva tadā jagrāha pāṇinā
english: One fair lady then took up with her right hand a jewel-studded bowl filled with drink.

sanskrit: rājahaṃsapratīkāśaṃ chatraṃ pūrṇaśaśiprabham sauvarṇadaṇḍam aparā gṛhītvā pṛṣṭhato yayau
english: Another took up a parasol resembling a royal swan, bright as the full moon, with a golden staff, and went behind him.

sanskrit: nidrāmadaparītākṣyo rāvaṇasyottamastriyaḥ anujagmuḥ patiṃ vīraṃ ghanaṃ vidyullatā iva
english: Rāvaṇa's noble wives, their eyes heavy with sleep and intoxication, followed their heroic lord as lightning-creepers follow a storm-cloud.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcīninādaṃ ca nūpurāṇāṃ ca niḥsvanam śuśrāva paramastrīṇāṃ sa kapir mārutātmajaḥ
english: Then the monkey, son of the Wind, heard the jingling of girdles and the tinkling of anklets of those foremost women.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpratimakarmāṇam acintyabalapauruṣam dvāradeśam anuprāptaṃ dadarśa hanumān kapiḥ
english: The monkey Hanumān saw him — that one of matchless deeds and inconceivable strength and valour — as he reached the gateway.

sanskrit: dīpikābhir anekābhiḥ samantād avabhāsitam gandhatailāvasiktābhir dhriyamāṇābhir agrataḥ
english: He was illuminated on all sides by numerous lamps soaked in fragrant oil and held aloft before him.

sanskrit: kāmadarpamadair yuktaṃ jihmatāmrāyatekṣaṇam samakṣam iva kandarpam apaviddha śarāsanam
english: His eyes oblique, coppery, and wide — suffused with desire, pride, and passion — he appeared like Kāmadeva himself who had cast aside his bow.

sanskrit: mathitāmṛtaphenābham arajo vastram uttamam salīlam anukarṣantaṃ vimuktaṃ saktam aṅgade
english: His finest garment — white as the foam of churned nectar and free of dust — trailed gracefully behind him, caught loosely on his armlet.

sanskrit: taṃ patraviṭape līnaḥ patrapuṣpaghanāvṛtaḥ samīpam upasaṃkrāntaṃ nidhyātum upacakrame
english: Concealed in the foliage of a branch, hidden by the dense mass of leaves and flowers, Hanumān began to observe him as he drew near.

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇaś ca tato dadarśa kapikuñjaraḥ rūpayauvanasaṃpannā rāvaṇasya varastriyaḥ
english: As he looked on, that elephant among monkeys saw Rāvaṇa's beautiful women, endowed with beauty and youth.

sanskrit: tābhiḥ parivṛto rājā surūpābhir mahāyaśāḥ tanmṛgadvijasaṃghuṣṭaṃ praviṣṭaḥ pramadāvanam
english: The king of great renown, encircled by those lovely women, entered the pleasure-grove resounding with the calls of deer and birds.

sanskrit: kṣībo vicitrābharaṇaḥ śaṅkukarṇo mahābalaḥ tena viśravasaḥ putraḥ sa dṛṣṭo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Intoxicated, adorned with variegated ornaments, with sharp ears, and greatly powerful — this son of Viśravas, the lord of rākṣasas, was thus seen.

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ paramanārībhis tārābhir iva candramāḥ taṃ dadarśa mahātejās tejovantaṃ mahākapiḥ
english: Surrounded by those foremost women as the moon is by stars, the greatly resplendent great monkey beheld him — that one of great splendour.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo 'yaṃ mahābāhur iti saṃcintya vānaraḥ avapluto mahātejā hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: "This is the mighty-armed Rāvaṇa" — thinking thus, the greatly resplendent Hanumān, son of the Wind, leapt down.

sanskrit: sa tathāpy ugratejāḥ san nirdhūtas tasya tejasā patraguhyāntare sakto hanūmān saṃvṛto 'bhavat
english: Yet though himself of fierce energy, Hanumān was overwhelmed by Rāvaṇa's radiance and remained hidden, clinging concealed within the shelter of a leafy hollow.

sanskrit: sa tām asitakeśāntāṃ suśroṇīṃ saṃhatastanīm didṛkṣur asitāpāṅgīm upāvartata rāvaṇaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa turned and drew near, wishing to behold her — she of dark tresses, beautiful hips, full breasts, and dark-cornered eyes.

sanskrit: tasminn eva tataḥ kāle rājaputrī tv aninditā rūpayauvanasaṃpannaṃ bhūṣaṇottamabhūṣitam
english: At that very moment the blameless princess — she who is endowed with beauty and youth — saw him adorned with the finest of ornaments:

sanskrit: tato dṛṣṭvaiva vaidehī rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam prāvepata varārohā pravāte kadalī yathā
english: upon seeing Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, Vaidehī — she of noble stature — trembled like a plantain tree in the wind.

sanskrit: ūrubhyām udaraṃ chādya bāhubhyāṃ ca payodharau upaviṣṭā viśālākṣī rudantī varavarṇinī
english: Covering her belly with her thighs and her breasts with her arms, the wide-eyed, fair-complexioned woman sat weeping.

sanskrit: daśagrīvas tu vaidehīṃ rakṣitāṃ rākṣasīgaṇaiḥ dadarśa dīnāṃ duḥkhārtaṃ nāvaṃ sannām ivārṇave
english: Daśagrīva beheld Vaidehī, guarded by the throng of rākṣasī women — wretched, tormented by grief, like a sinking boat upon the ocean.

sanskrit: asaṃvṛtāyām āsīnāṃ dharaṇyāṃ saṃśitavratām chinnāṃ prapatitāṃ bhūmau śākhām iva vanaspateḥ malamaṇḍanadigdhāṅgīṃ maṇḍanārhām amaṇḍitām
english: Seated on the bare ground, firm in her vow, her limbs smeared with dirt in lieu of adornment — she who deserved adornment yet wore none — like a broken branch fallen to the earth from a forest tree.

sanskrit: samīpaṃ rājasiṃhasya rāmasya viditātmanaḥ saṃkalpahayasaṃyuktair yāntīm iva manorathaiḥ
english: She seemed to travel on the horses of resolve and longing toward the presence of Rāma — that lion among kings, the knower of the self.

sanskrit: śuṣyantīṃ rudatīm ekāṃ dhyānaśokaparāyaṇām duḥkhasyāntam apaśyantīṃ rāmāṃ rāmam anuvratām
english: Wasting away, weeping, alone, absorbed in meditation and grief, seeing no end to her sorrow — she who was utterly devoted to Rāma.

sanskrit: veṣṭamānām athāviṣṭāṃ pannagendravadhūm iva dhūpyamānāṃ graheṇeva rohiṇīṃ dhūmaketunā
english: Writhing and afflicted — like the wife of the serpent-lord in his coils — tormented as Rohiṇī is by a comet in the grip of a planet.

sanskrit: vṛttaśīle kule jātām ācāravati dhārmike punaḥ saṃskāram āpannāṃ jātam iva ca duṣkule
english: Born of a family of noble conduct, in a lineage virtuous and righteous — yet brought to such refinement as though born anew in a low family.

sanskrit: sannām iva mahākīrtiṃ śraddhām iva vimānitām prajñām iva parikṣīṇām āśāṃ pratihatām iva
english: Like great fame that has faded, like faith that has been dishonoured, like wisdom that has dwindled, like hope that has been thwarted.

sanskrit: āyatīm iva vidhvastām ājñāṃ pratihatām iva dīptām iva diśaṃ kāle pūjām apahṛtām iva
english: Like a prosperous future destroyed, like a command countermanded, like a direction blazing bright whose time has passed, like an act of worship stolen away.

sanskrit: padminīm iva vidhvastāṃ hataśūrāṃ camūm iva prabhām iva tapodhvastām upakṣīṇām ivāpagām
english: Like a lotus-pond laid waste, like an army whose heroes have been slain, like a radiance undone by ascetic's curse, like a river running thin.

sanskrit: vedīm iva parāmṛṣṭāṃ śāntām agniśikhām iva paurṇamāsīm iva niśāṃ rāhugrastendumaṇḍalām
english: Like a sacrificial altar defiled, like a flame of fire extinguished, like the full-moon night whose lunar disc is seized by Rāhu.

sanskrit: utkṛṣṭaparṇakamalāṃ vitrāsitavihaṃgamām hastihastaparāmṛṣṭām ākulāṃ padminīm iva
english: Like a lotus-pond thrown into confusion — its lotus leaves plucked out, its birds frightened away, disturbed by an elephant's trunk.

sanskrit: patiśokāturāṃ śuṣkāṃ nadīṃ visrāvitām iva parayā mṛjayā hīnāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe niśām iva
english: Tormented by grief for her husband, withered — like a river drained dry, bereft of all luster, like the night of the dark fortnight.

sanskrit: sukumārīṃ sujātāṅgīṃ ratnagarbhagṛhocitām tapyamānām ivoṣṇena mṛṇālīm aciroddhṛtām
english: Delicate, with perfectly formed limbs, fit to dwell in a gem-studded inner chamber — yet scorched as a lotus-stalk only recently uprooted burns in the heat.

sanskrit: gṛhītāmālitāṃ stambhe yūthapena vinākṛtām niḥśvasantīṃ suduḥkhārtāṃ gajarājavadhūm iva
english: Seized and chained to a post, separated from the lord of the herd — sighing, deeply tormented by grief — like the wife of the elephant-king.

sanskrit: ekayā dīrghayā veṇyā śobhamānām ayatnataḥ nīlayā nīradāpāye vanarājyā mahīm iva
english: Beautiful without effort, adorned by a single long dark braid — like the earth at the passing of the rain-clouds, clothed in a kingdom of forest.

sanskrit: upavāsena śokena dhyānena ca bhayena ca parikṣīṇāṃ kṛśāṃ dīnām alpāhārāṃ tapodhanām
english: Wasted away by fasting, grief, meditation, and fear — emaciated, wretched, eating little, rich only in austerity.

sanskrit: āyācamānāṃ duḥkhārtāṃ prāñjaliṃ devatām iva bhāvena raghumukhyasya daśagrīvaparābhavam
english: Afflicted with grief, hands folded like a deity imploring — she prayed with all her being for Rāma, the foremost of the Raghus, to vanquish Daśagrīva.

sanskrit: samīkṣamāṇāṃ rudatīm aninditāṃ supakṣmatāmrāyataśuklalocanām anuvratāṃ rāmam atīva maithilīṃ pralobhayām āsa vadhāya rāvaṇaḥ
english: Gazing and weeping, blameless, her eyes fringed with fine lashes — coppery, wide, and white — utterly devoted to Rāma: Maithilī thus inflamed Rāvaṇa exceedingly, to his own destruction.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ parivṛtāṃ dīnāṃ nirānandāṃ tapasvinīm sākārair madhurair vākyair nyadarśayata rāvaṇaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa addressed her — who was surrounded, wretched, joyless, and afflicted — with words that were sweet and full of expressive gestures.

sanskrit: māṃ dṛṣṭvā nāganāsorugūhamānā stanodaram adarśanam ivātmānaṃ bhayān netuṃ tvam icchasi
english: "Upon seeing me, you cover your thighs and belly with your arms, as if wishing out of fear to render yourself invisible."

sanskrit: kāmaye tvāṃ viśālākṣi bahumanyasva māṃ priye sarvāṅgaguṇasaṃpanne sarvalokamanohare
english: "I desire you, wide-eyed one; hold me in high regard, my dear — you who are endowed with perfection of every limb, enchanting to all the worlds."

sanskrit: neha ke cin manuṣyā vā rākṣasāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ vyapasarpatu te sīte bhayaṃ mattaḥ samutthitam
english: "There are no humans here, nor rākṣasas who take any shape they will. Let the fear that has arisen in you from me depart, O Sītā."

sanskrit: svadharme rakṣasāṃ bhīru sarvathaiṣa na saṃśayaḥ gamanaṃ vā parastrīṇāṃ haraṇaṃ saṃpramathya vā
english: "Among rākṣasas, O timid one, this is in every way their proper law — beyond doubt: either going to the wives of others or carrying them away by force."

sanskrit: evaṃ caitad akāmāṃ ca na tvāṃ sprakṣyāmi maithili kāmaṃ kāmaḥ śarīre me yathākāmaṃ pravartatām
english: "Yet being such, I will not touch you against your will, O Maithilī; let desire play freely in my body as it pleases — but I will not act."

sanskrit: devi neha bhayaṃ kāryaṃ mayi viśvasihi priye praṇayasva ca tattvena maivaṃ bhūḥ śokalālasā
english: "Lady, there is nothing to fear here; place your trust in me, my dear, and give me your love truly — do not thus languish in sorrow."

sanskrit: ekaveṇī dharāśayyā dhyānaṃ malinam ambaram asthāne 'py upavāsaś ca naitāny aupayikāni te
english: "A single braid, a bed upon the ground, meditation, soiled garments, and fasting even without purpose — these are not fitting for you."

sanskrit: vicitrāṇi ca mālyāni candanāny agarūṇi ca vividhāni ca vāsāṃsi divyāny ābharaṇāni ca
english: "Colourful garlands, sandalwood paste, aloe-wood, garments of many kinds, and divine ornaments —"

sanskrit: mahārhāṇi ca pānāni yānāni śayanāni ca gītaṃ nṛttaṃ ca vādyaṃ ca labha māṃ prāpya maithili
english: "— the most precious drinks, conveyances, beds, song, dance, and music: obtain all these by accepting me, O Maithilī."

sanskrit: strīratnam asi maivaṃ bhūḥ kuru gātreṣu bhūṣaṇam māṃ prāpya tu kathaṃ hi syās tvam anarhā suvigrahe
english: "You are a jewel among women — do not be thus; adorn your limbs with ornaments. How could you be unworthy, you of such beauty, having attained me?"

sanskrit: idaṃ te cārusaṃjātaṃ yauvanaṃ vyativartate yad atītaṃ punar naiti srotaḥ śīghram apām iva
english: "This your youth — so exquisitely arisen — is passing away; that which is past never returns, like the swift current of waters."

sanskrit: tvāṃ kṛtvoparato manye rūpakartā sa viśvakṛt na hi rūpopamā tv anyā tavāsti śubhadarśane
english: "I believe that having made you, the creator of form — the maker of the universe — rested from his labour; for no other exists equal to you in beauty, O fair to behold."

sanskrit: tvāṃ samāsādya vaidehi rūpayauvanaśālinīm kaḥ pumān ativarteta sākṣād api pitāmahaḥ
english: "Having encountered you, O Vaidehī — resplendent with beauty and youth — what man could remain unmoved? Even the Grandfather himself, Brahmā, could not."

sanskrit: yad yat paśyāmi te gātraṃ śītāṃśusadṛśānane tasmiṃs tasmin pṛthuśroṇi cakṣur mama nibadhyate
english: "On each and every part of your body that I behold — O you whose face is like the cool-rayed moon, O broad-hipped one — my gaze becomes fixed."

sanskrit: bhava maithili bhāryā me moham enaṃ visarjaya bahvīnām uttamastrīṇāṃ mamāgramahiṣī bhava
english: "Become my wife, O Maithilī — cast aside this folly; become the chief queen among the many foremost women I possess."

sanskrit: lokebhyo yāni ratnāni saṃpramathyāhṛtāni me tāni te bhīru sarvāṇi rājyaṃ caitad ahaṃ ca te
english: "All the jewels that have been seized and brought by me from the worlds — all of these are yours, O timid one; this kingdom is yours, and I am yours."

sanskrit: vijitya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ nānānagaramālinīm janakāya pradāsyāmi tava hetor vilāsini
english: "Having conquered the entire earth, garlanded with its many cities, I shall give it to Janaka for your sake, O graceful one."

sanskrit: neha paśyāmi loke 'nyaṃ yo me pratibalo bhavet paśya me sumahad vīryam apratidvandvam āhave
english: "I see no other in this world who could be my equal in strength; behold my exceedingly great valour — without adversary in battle."

sanskrit: asakṛt saṃyuge bhagnā mayā vimṛditadhvajāḥ aśaktāḥ pratyanīkeṣu sthātuṃ mama surāsurāḥ
english: "Again and again in battle, gods and asuras alike have been routed by me, their banners crushed — unable to stand against my forces."

sanskrit: iccha māṃ kriyatām adya pratikarma tavottamam saprabhāṇy avasajjantāṃ tavāṅge bhūṣaṇāni ca sādhu paśyāmi te rūpaṃ saṃyuktaṃ pratikarmaṇā
english: "Desire me; let the finest adornment be done to you today; let the radiant ornaments be fastened upon your limbs — I see your beauty perfectly suited to such adorning."

sanskrit: pratikarmābhisaṃyuktā dākṣiṇyena varānane bhuṅkṣva bhogān yathākāmaṃ piba bhīru ramasva ca yatheṣṭaṃ ca prayaccha tvaṃ pṛthivīṃ vā dhanāni ca
english: "Adorned with all manner of adornment, gracious in bearing, O fair-faced one — enjoy pleasures as you wish, drink, take delight, O timid one, and bestow as you please — even the earth and its wealth."

sanskrit: lalasva mayi visrabdhā dhṛṣṭam ājñāpayasva ca matprabhāvāl lalantyāś ca lalantāṃ bāndhavās tava
english: "Revel in me with confidence and boldly command me; and through my power, as you flourish, let your kinsmen also flourish."

sanskrit: ṛddhiṃ mamānupaśya tvaṃ śriyaṃ bhadre yaśaś ca me kiṃ kariṣyasi rāmeṇa subhage cīravāsasā
english: "Behold my prosperity, my glory, and my renown, O fortunate one; what will you do with Rāma, O beautiful one — Rāma who wears bark-cloth?"

sanskrit: nikṣiptavijayo rāmo gataśrīr vanagocaraḥ vratī sthaṇḍilaśāyī ca śaṅke jīvati vā na vā
english: "Rāma has renounced his victory, his glory is gone, he wanders the forest, bound by a vow, sleeping on the bare ground — I doubt whether he even lives."

sanskrit: na hi vaidehi rāmas tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ vāpy upalapsyate puro balākair asitair meghair jyotsnām ivāvṛtām
english: "Rāma will neither see you nor obtain you, O Vaidehī — as a swarm of dark cranes before the clouds conceals the moonlight."

sanskrit: na cāpi mama hastāt tvāṃ prāptum arhati rāghavaḥ hiraṇyakaśipuḥ kīrtim indrahastagatām iva
english: "Nor does Rāghava deserve to recover you from my hands — as Hiraṇyakaśipu could not recover the glory that had passed into Indra's hands."

sanskrit: cārusmite cārudati cārunetre vilāsini mano harasi me bhīru suparṇaḥ pannagaṃ yathā
english: "O you of lovely smile, lovely teeth, lovely eyes — O graceful one — you steal my mind, O timid one, as Garuḍa seizes a serpent."

sanskrit: kliṣṭakauśeyavasanāṃ tanvīm apy analaṃkṛtām tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sveṣu dāreṣu ratiṃ nopalabhāmy aham
english: "Having seen you — slender, unadorned, clad in a soiled silk garment — I find no pleasure in my own wives."

sanskrit: antaḥpuranivāsinyaḥ striyaḥ sarvaguṇānvitāḥ yāvantyo mama sarvāsām aiśvaryaṃ kuru jānaki
english: "However many women dwell in my inner apartments, endowed with every virtue — exercise sovereignty over all of them, O Jānakī."

sanskrit: mama hy asitakeśānte trailokyapravarāḥ striyaḥ tās tvāṃ paricariṣyanti śriyam apsaraso yathā
english: "For among my dark-tressed women are the foremost ladies of the three worlds; they shall wait upon you as the Apsarases attend upon Śrī."

sanskrit: yāni vaiśravaṇe subhru ratnāni ca dhanāni ca tāni lokāṃś ca suśroṇi māṃ ca bhuṅkṣva yathāsukham
english: "The jewels and wealth that belong to Vaiśravaṇa — those, and the worlds themselves, and me, O lovely-browed, broad-hipped one — enjoy all at your pleasure."

sanskrit: na rāmas tapasā devi na balena na vikramaiḥ na dhanena mayā tulyas tejasā yaśasāpi vā
english: "Rāma is not my equal, O lady — not in asceticism, not in strength, not in valour, not in wealth, not in energy, nor in glory."

sanskrit: piba vihara ramasva bhuṅkṣva bhogān dhananicayaṃ pradiśāmi medinīṃ ca mayi lala lalane yathāsukhaṃ tvaṃ tvayi ca sametya lalantu bāndhavās te
english: "Drink, roam freely, take delight, enjoy pleasures; I give you wealth in abundance and the earth itself — revel in me at your pleasure, O graceful one, and let your kinsmen gather around you and revel in you."

sanskrit: kusumitatarujālasaṃtatāni bhramarayutāni samudratīrajāni kanakavimalahārabhūṣitāṅgī vihara mayā saha bhīru kānanāni
english: "Your limbs adorned with necklaces of pure gold, roam with me through the forests along the seashore — forests draped in networks of flowering trees, humming with bees, O timid one."
